The Section on Detailed Exposition, Chapter Sixteen: Convergence (Sampāta)
The Convergence of the Mode of Conveying Application.
In this context, what is the convergence of the mode of conveying application?
“Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded...”
Having right intention as his range,
with right view as his primary concern,
and having understood arising and passing away;
“A bhikkhu overcome by sloth and torpor would abandon all states of woe.
Therefore, “of one whose mind is guarded” is the foundation for the three types of good conduct; when the mind is guarded, bodily action, verbal action, and mental action are likewise guarded.
"One who has right view as the foremost" means that when right view is developed, the Noble Eightfold Path becomes developed.
For what reason?
Because from right view, right intention arises; from right intention, right speech arises; from right speech...
Right action arises; from right action, right livelihood arises; from right livelihood, right effort arises;
from right effort, right mindfulness arises; from right mindfulness, right concentration arises;
from right concentration, right liberation arises; and from right liberation, the knowledge and vision of right liberation arises.
This is the person without residue and the element of nibbāna without residue.
The application of the method of coordination is concluded.
Thus said the Venerable Mahākaccāyana.
“First, having surveyed the directions from the ‘eye of the quarters,’ one should summarize the sixteen modes of conveying by means of the ‘hook.’”
"Explain the Sutta by means of the three methods.
The section on the Modes of Conveying (Hārasampāta) is concluded.
